name: Name
body: Captain Braghen Ragemonger stood at the prow of the Purgatory and watched the shoreline drift sluggishly by. They’d sailed up from Alchiere, into the Bay of Cygnar, and then inland along the Black River seeking soft targets they could easily overwhelm and plunder. That not a single Cygnaran vessel had challenged or even noticed them would be called luck by most, but Braghen knew it was simply the curse he’d suffered under for the better part of two decades. No matter how dangerous a situation, no matter how dire the odds against him, no matter how much he wanted to end his life on the point of an enemy’s blade, he survived, he triumphed, and his damnable legend grew. "Ah, there you are, Great One," Coxswain Hudgum said as he clambered up from the hold. Braghen rolled his eyes. "Hudgum, what have I told you about that?" "About what, Mighty One?" the pyg said as he joined his captain next to the gunwales. "My name is Braghen. Not great one, not mighty one, and not any of the bloody titles you and the rest of the crew have seen fit to inflict upon me."

name: Name
body: "Oh, uh, my apologies, great . . . Braghen," the pyg said, his face downcast. Braghen took a deep breath and let it out slowly. It whistled through the filed points of his teeth. "I’m sorry, Hudgum. I’m just . . . restless. We haven’t seen anything so much as a garbage scow since we left the Bay of Cygnar." "Then I might have something that will cheer you, uh, Captain," Hudgum said, settling on a title that didn’t make Braghen want to chew his little head off. "Well?" "One of the sky raiders has reported something interesting a few miles up the river," Hudgum said. "The wreckage of two ships." Braghen brightened. Wreckage meant battle, and battle meant he could quiet the howling voices of long-dead friends and kithmates that stormed through his brain every hour of every day. Only the very immediate threat of death offered him any peace. "Did they identify the ships?" Hudgum nodded. "Orgoth." *** Anticipating battle, Braghen summoned the crew of the Purgatory to the main deck—it was a motley assembly of trollkin and pyg warriors armed with a similarly motley collection of cutlasses, pistols, belaying clubs, and harpoons. Among them loomed a pair of reef trolls, Huk and Muk, and the monstrous hulking form of Mast-Ripper, Braghen’s deepborn dire troll.

name: Name
body: Ahead, the remains of the two ships clogged the riverway. A mast, cracked in half and draped in red sails like a bloody shroud, jutted from the water beside an upturned and shattered hull. As the Purgatory drifted among the wreckage, Braghen saw bodies in the water clad in the distinctive fur and leather of Orgoth raiders. Their wounds, what he could see of them, were unlike those he was accustomed to finding in ship-to-ship combat. No gaping cuts or dismemberments, no mangled bodies from spell or cannon fire. Death had taken these Orgoth with uncanny precision, leaving their corpses eerily intact. "Ship ahead," the lookout in the crow’s nest called out from above. Braghen hefted his harpoon, Whaler, and raced to the prow. A black vessel sliced through the water toward them. It was no ocean-going ship—the graceful curves of its shallow hull would not withstand rough water—and resembled a great flat-decked barge. It moved without sail or oars and was propelled instead by a single paddle wheel that drove it forward like a great onyx arrow.

name: Name
body: Other members of the crew joined Braghen. "What is it, Farrowbane?" one sailor asked. "Have you have seen their like before, Sharkslayer?" said another. Braghen gritted his teeth as more trollkin bombarded him with questions and titles. "We’ve come far enough up the river, we could be in Ios," Hudgum said. "Eldritch," Braghen said, his excitement building. He could now see the sailors on the approaching ship—their lithe angular frames, their armor both shockingly alien and strikingly baroque. As the ship drew nearer, he saw withered faces beneath silver helms, the grayish tint of unnatural flesh in the gaps of armor, and, moreover, he could sense an otherness that filled him with both dread and the lust for battle. "Orders, Captain?" Hudgum said. Braghen reached out to the reef trolls and his dire troll, connecting to their feral minds and letting their primal rage wipe away his own troublesome thoughts. His shark familiar, Kharka, swam in the Black River below, and Braghen ached to join him.

name: Name
body: "I will attack from the river with the trolls," Braghen said. "Get the cannon crews busy. When that ship’s in range, open fire but do not board her." "He is the Wavekiller!" a trollkin crewmember shouted, eyes wide. Others repeated this new title with similar reverence. Wavekiller. Wavekiller. Wavekiller. "Wait. You will face the enemy alone?" Hudgum said, his tiny features pinched in alarm. Braghen offered Hudgum a shark-toothed smile and dove into the dark water below. ***

name: Name
body: The eldritch fought in silence. The silence of death, Braghen thought as he threw himself against a line of soulless elves wielding huge shields and wicked glaives. He skewered one with his harpoon, but his foe uttered no sound, no cry of pain or anguish as the saw-toothed spear ripped through him. The soulless slipped to the deck. Another grim soldier took his place. Behind Braghen, the reef trolls, Ruk and Muk, had engaged one of the Iosan warjacks, a gaunt, spindly thing armed with a shield and sword. The trolls hammered at the machine with boarding axes the size of ship oars and had damaged it considerably. Elsewhere on the deck of the elven ship, Mast-Ripper, the deepborn dire troll, was busy stuffing bits of wrecked myrmidon into his massive gullet. The troll’s immense disappointment that each morsel neither screamed nor bled as he chewed them to wreckage echoed back through his link with Braghen. After a few volleys of cannon fire, a good portion of the crew of the Purgatory had boarded the eldritch vessel against Braghen’s orders, and the battle had turned into a true melee. He wanted to lose himself in the glorious chaos of it, to burn away the pain of past failures in a conflagration of rage, but if he gave himself over to the battle madness to seek the death he so desperately wanted, the crew of the Purgatory would suffer.

name: Name
body: More soulless elves surged onto the deck, and Braghen realized they would soon be overwhelmed. He was about to sound the retreat to save as many of his crew as possible when she appeared, a vision of graceful destruction, a great sword in each hand, purple banners and snake-like braids of silver hair flying about her as she slashed through Braghen’s pirates. As the eldritch captain moved across the deck, the weapons of her fallen foes sprang into the air around her in a whirlwind of blades. The crew of the Purgatory prepared to throw themselves into battle with the terrible apparition in steel, and Braghen knew dozens would die if he didn’t act now. "Retreat!" he called out. "Back to the Purgatory!" His pirates began a fighting retreat to the prow of the ship where boarding ramps had been laid across the space between the Purgatory and the eldritch vessel, but not enough would escape before the eldritch commander cut them to pieces. Braghen had to buy his crew more time, and he saw only one way to do it. He summoned the arcane strength in his blood. Tingling power filled his limbs. He launched himself into the air, flying over the melee to slam into the deck before the whirling blades of the eldritch commander.

name: Name
body:
She came at him in a cyclone of destruction, her great swords hammering down on his harpoon as he desperately attempted to parry them. She evaded his parries with relative ease, slashing open his right arm, his left leg, then driving one of her blades clean through his abdomen, impaling him. It halted her frenzy of attacks for a heartbeat, and Braghen yanked himself up her blade and sank his shark-like teeth into her shoulder, biting clean through the steel. Her flesh was ash on his tongue, but as she attempted to rip free, he hung on doggedly, holding her in place.
The eldritch commander jerked and writhed, trying to dislodge Braghen’s jaws from her shoulder. Finally, she let go of her blades, placed both hands on the sides of Braghen’s head, and with surprising strength, tore him loose and shoved him to the deck. With a cry of fury, she raised both hands into the air, and the weapons of fallen eldritch and trollkin scattered across the ship leapt into the air and rained down upon Braghen, ripping through his arms and legs and pinning him to the deck.

name: Name
body: "Slay them all!" the eldritch commander roared and pointed at the trollkin fleeing back to the Purgatory. Horrified, Braghen tore free from the weapons fastening him to the deck and struggled to his feet. "Stop," he croaked, blood spilling from his mouth. The eldritch commander said nothing, and her soldiers continued to bear down on the crew of the Purgatory, who had turned to make a stand. Seconds before the two sides met in combat once more, she held up a hand—and her soulless halted their advance. Braghen seized on the opportunity and wrapped his hands around the hilt of the eldritch commander’s great sword that still transfixed his body. With a pained grunt, he pulled the blade from his flesh and offered the gore-stained sword to its owner. "Peace. Please." The eldritch commander took a step back, her posture relaxing slightly. She stood silently for a moment, then reached out and snatched her sword from Braghen’s grasp. "Why have you attacked us?" she said, her voice a grating whisper, like wind through a sepulcher.

name: Name
body: Braghen shook his head. "Because I am a fool." The eldritch nodded, clearly agreeing. "And what is your name, fool?" "I am called Braghen Ragemonger, lately of the Southern Kriels." The eldritch flicked Braghen’s blood from her blade then lowered it. "You stand before Scyrafael of House Eyvreyn, Nis-Issyr of Desolation. If you are part of the Southern Kriels, then you are indeed a fool for attacking a potential ally. What am I to do with you?" "Do with me what you think is just," Braghen said. "But let my crew go." Scyrafael stared at Braghen, her yellow eyes penetrating and brutally appraising. "I have heard of you, you know." "He is the Wavekiller!" a trollkin pirate shouted from somewhere. "Farrowbane!" cried another. "Sharkslayer! Croakfriend! Bladebiter!" Braghen winced. "Impressive titles," Scyrafael said. "But I have another for you. I name you Deathchaser. Your soul cries out for it. Why?" "I seek peace," Braghen whispered, surprised by the horrid need in his voice. "I see no other way to attain it."

name: Name
body:
Scyrafael laughed mirthlessly. "You must trust me when I say there is no peace in death. It is no release from pain; it merely continues the pain we have wrought in life."
Braghen glanced around at the destruction littering the deck of the eldritch ship. "If my life will atone for the pain I have wrought here, then take it."
"No, Braghen Ragemonger, I will not give you what you seek," Scyrafael said. "But I will give you a task, one you must remain among the living to complete."
She nodded at one of the elven warriors nearby, and the Iosan disappeared into the hold. He returned minutes later holding an object swaddled in cloth and leather, his undead features pinched in obvious pain. He laid the bundle at Braghen’s feet.
"We found this in the hold of one of the Orgoth ships," Scyrafael said. "It is an artifact of terrible power. A weapon that can be used against those who have, shall we say, forsaken mortality."
Braghen picked up the bundle, unwrapped it, and saw a small obelisk of black stone, perhaps three feet in length, its surface carved with blood-red runes that seemed to swirl and writhe of their own accord. It made him feel seasick to look at it. He covered it again. "What is it?"

name: Name
body: "A key, "Scyrafael said, "to a door that must never be opened.’ "What must I do with it?" Braghen asked, trying to reconcile the strange and abrupt turn of events. "Take it with you. When you reach the Meredius, cast it into the ocean, so that it might never be found. That is what I require of you. That is your penance. Do this, and perhaps someday I will call you ally." *** Braghen watched the Iosan vessel fade into the distance as he and the Purgatory headed toward the sea. Part of him wanted to honor Scyrafael’s request, but if the Orgoth artifact were a key, then perhaps the door it unlocked held secrets that would aid the Southern Kriels, perhaps all of western Immoren, against the Orgoth. He owed greater debts than that which he now owed the eldritch. "Captain," Coxswain Hudgum said and scampered up to the railing beside Braghen, "I am happy to report the ship’s surgeon says we didn’t lose anyone, just a few arms and legs that’ll grow back as good as new." Braghen nodded. At least his latest attempted tryst with death had left no trollkin bodies in its wake. Not even his own.

name: Name
body: "Uh, I also want to warn you about something, Captain," Hudgum said. "The boys have a new title for you. Thought you should hear it from me first.’ "Of course," Braghen said. "What is it this time?" "Well, seeing as you convinced that eldritch to stop fighting and let us go, they’re calling you, uh, Deathtamer." Braghen smiled at how his crew was choosing to remember the events that had just transpired. "You know, Hudgum, that one’s not bad."

name: Name
body:
Warchief Bagadibawm raced through the jungle, his vorogger, Guggermug, crashing through the underbrush alongside him. Bagadibawm could hear the interlopers not far behind, trying to follow his winding path through the tangled briar of the Alchiere rainforest. Interlopers into Firetongue territory were nothing new. Bagadibawm had dealt with Skorne slavers, lethean marauders, and most recently the great influx of trollkin from the north. These new invaders, however, were more determined than usual: Orgoth clad in steel and fur and leather, leading great beasts and calling upon fearful magic.
Bagadibawm halted his meandering flight beneath the soaring branches of a goa tree and reached into the pouch at his waist. He removed a black stone obelisk covered in writhing red symbols. The inky darkness and geometric shape of the thing brought a chirp of distaste from him. The thing was unnatural, antithetical to life, and it stood out in stark contrast to the fecund abundance of the great jungle.

name: Name
body:
The Orgoth wanted the artifact, had risked the endless ocean and now the trackless jungle to acquire it. The trollkin battle chieftain Braghen Ragemonger had claimed the item on one of his many treks to the north and had brought it to Bagadibawm and the great sorceress Mawga’Bawza to divine its secrets, hoping it could be used as a weapon against the enemies of his people.
Bagadibawm and Mawga’Bawza had swiftly divined that the obelisk was a thing of evil, a harbinger of destruction, and a gateway to further horrors. Before they could inform Ragemonger of the evil he had brought into their midst, the Orgoth had arrived, drawn to the foul energies of the artifact like a hungry vorogger to rotting flesh. They had attacked Bagadibawm’s encampment in force, but instead of meeting the invaders in direct battle, he’d commanded his people to scatter into the jungle. Fighting an enemy on that enemy’s terms was always foolish. Let the Orgoth follow his warriors into the rainforest. Let them taste war among the trees.

name: Name
body: The sound of rhythmic drumming and a low susurrus of croaking chants to the north brought a low warble of pleasure from Bagadibawm, and he set off to join the dance. *** The Firetongue Warrior totem stood at the center of the clearing, a looming presence of ironwood and magic. The holy flames of Kaiwaba blazed upon the statue’s headdress and torches, and around it danced a dozen bullcroaks. Most were fire spitters, sturdy warriors with kegs of naphtha strapped to their backs and armed with warclubs and shields. They danced and gyrated, croaking the warriors’ song, and the sound of it filled Bagadibawm with joy. When the warchief entered the clearing, the largest of the bullcroaks, a fugue walker called Crikkok, stepped away from the dance and approached. He was massive, his skin a mottled green with iron-hard scutes at his shoulder and neck. His body swarmed with brightly colored frogs, each bearing a beneficial toxin available with a flick of the fugue walker’s tongue. He gripped a pair of toclu warclubs, flames dancing along their spiked lengths.

name: Name
body: "Warchief," Crikkok said, "we are ready. Are the interlopers close?" "Right behind me," Bagadibawm said and croaked laughter. "They blunder through the jungle like blind children, but they will see the flames." "And they will burn in them," Crikkok said. "Guggermug and I will join the fight, but we are to sting them, then retreat, make them follow me and this damnable artifact until the jungle has chewed them down to the stump," Bagadibawm said. "Understood?" Crikkok’s long pink tongue flicked across the body of a bright yellow toad on his shoulder. His eyes went hazy, and he loosed a low, reverberating war croak. "We may do a bit more than sting them, Warchief." *** Bagadibawm assumed the Orgoth leader was human, though it was difficult to tell beneath the steel mask he wore. Pale flesh peeked out from beneath gaps in the blood-red cloth or the iron mail, its pallor sickly, unhealthy, death-like. With lurid green flames rising from his flail and outstretched hand, the Orgoth warlord burst into the clearing, shouting in his alien tongue, and the jungle disgorged a stream of misshapen figures behind him, all assuredly not human. Their weapons, whether they be sword or axe, glowed with evil radiance, and the distant sound of screaming could be heard as the Orgoth soldiers charged ahead.

name: Name
body:
A great beast crashed through the forest to stand beside the Orgoth leader, a monstrosity of steel and flesh, a creature twisted into its current form to serve the foul and incomprehensible purposes of its masters. It held a great cleaving blade in one gnarled fist while its other hand had been removed and replaced with steel pincer.
The fire spitters ended their dance and launched a volley of flaming naphtha at the invaders, scorching their bodies and sending a handful to the ground writhing in agony as holy flame consumed them.
Crikkok joined the battle next, and his war clubs split skulls with berserk fury, cleaving through steel and bone in explosions of fiery brilliance. The fugue walker’s booming song drowned out the screaming evil of the invaders’ blades. The fire spitters joined Crikkok with flaming club and shield, and soon the Firetongue Warrior towered over a swirling melee.
Bagadibawm and Guggermug waited on the other side of the totem, waited for what came next. With the Orgoth warriors distracted, their leader, sensing either Bagadibawm’s status or the relic he carried, called out.

name: Name
body: "Give me the key, creature," the Orgoth warlord said in passable trollkin. "Give it to me now, and some of your people may avoid the slaver’s lash." "What is your name, fiend?" Bagadibawm replied. The Orgoth warrior laughed behind his steel mask, distant and hollow. "I am Oriax, the Soul Slaver." "I look forward to carving your name into the goa tree where my tribe records their lesser deeds," Bagadibawm said. He held his war torches out, and they burst into nimbuses of flame. Guggermug bellowed in eager rage as the torchlight gleamed from his slimy skin, and Bagadibawm urged him forward, following close behind. The vorogger belched forth a ball of fire as he and Bagadibawm closed the distance between them and their foe. The fiery gobbet exploded against the chest of the Orgoth monstrosity, driving it back with a howl of fury. Bagadibawm reached Oriax and lashed out with his torches, singeing the Orgoth warlord’s armor and drawing a hiss of pain from the enemy. The warlord swung his flail in reply, and Bagadibawm ducked beneath it, the air of its passing trailing a foul reek.

name: Name
body:
Through his link with Guggermug, Bagadibawm saw the vorogger had joined battle with the Orgoth monstrosity, lashing out with its claws to rip bleeding furrows in the horror’s mottled hide. The return stroke from the monstrosity’s cleaver would have sliced any lesser beast in half, but the vorogger’s strange dense flesh turned the mortal wound into an aggravating scratch.
More Orgoth soldiers poured into the clearing, and Bagadibawm inflated his throat sac to its fullest and bellowed a high, warbling croak. The sound had two purposes. It was the call to retreat, and it would let Mawga’Bawza know he was on his way to the next chokepoint.
Bagadibawm rolled beneath another strike from Oriax’s flail and leaped away into the trees. He pulled Guggermug, grudgingly, from his own battle, and the vorogger launched itself into the air and landed at Bagadibawm’s side with a ground-shaking thud.
The surviving fire spitters disengaged and fled, leaving behind the body of Crikkok, lying torn and mangled and surrounded by no fewer than a dozen Orgoth corpses.

name: Name
body: *** Mawga’Bawza regarded Bagadibawm with a disapproving glare. The great sorceress squatted upon her galoportoise throne, her broad-brimmed hat shielding her face from the sun’s glare that shone down through the stand of goa trees. Ten spirit shamans crowded around Mawga’Bawza, their ceremonial Te masks set in rictus frowns of righteous anger. More fire spitters, some two dozen, danced around another Firetongue Warrior totem behind the sorcerer. "Did you kill any of them?" Mawga’Bawza said. "I am Bagadibawm, warchief, Skorne-slayer, lethean blight," Bagadibawm said, somewhat affronted. "Yes, yes, but did you kill any of them?" Mawga’Bawza said, motioning back toward the way Bagadibawm had come. "Of course," he said. "But they still follow and in force." Mawga’Bawza sighed and ambled forward on her galoportoise. "I told you we shouldn’t trust the trollkin. Now look what horror they have visited upon us." "Ragemonger could not have known the Orgoth would come looking for the artifact," Bagadibawm said, defending the fatalistic trollkin warlock as he usually did when the subject of their tenuous alliance was broached.

name: Name
body: "But they have, and our trollkin ally is nowhere to be found," Mawga’Bawza said then blew out a long grumbling sigh. "It matters not. I have done as you asked and reached out to Madrak for aid." "And?" "There is a ship waiting not far from here that will carry the artifact away from our lands and, Kaiwaba be merciful, these Orgoth will follow." "They’ll be here in moments." Mawga’Bawza laughed and slammed her fetish staff into the ground. "And when they arrive, we will give them a scorching welcome." *** Bagadibawm emerged from the jungle onto a narrow strip of sandy beach. The sea stretched to the horizon, the setting sun sliding into the water like the fiery eye of Kaiwaba. A three-masted ship was anchored fifty feet off shore, and a ragged collection of rowboats and launches had been pulled up onto the sand. A dozen or so trollkin stood around the boats, though one stood out from the rest. He was tall, broadly built, and dressed in strange finery Bagadibawm would normally associate with humans. Bottles of spirits were tied to his breeches and jacket, and a tricorn hat sat upon his head at a drunken angle. The trollkin had a long, curved blade in one hand and what appeared to be a tankard of ale in the other. He gesticulated wildly with both, as he spoke to what Bagadibawm assumed was his crew.

name: Name
body:
The warchief started forward with Guggermug in tow. The trollkin saw them coming and strode forward to meet them.
"That’s a bloody big frog," the trollkin captain said, squinting at Guggermug. "He really is there, right?"
Bagadibawm blinked in confusion. "Are . . . are you the one sent by Madrak?"
"Oh, my apologies," the trollkin said and bowed, spilling his ale and causing Bagadibawm to leap away from the errant sweep of his saber. "I am Commodore Foulblood, and I and my armada are at your service."
"Armada?" Bagadibawm said, eying the single ship and the tiny collection of boats.
Foulblood pointed back over his shoulder. "Yes, my armada. Right there."
Bagadibawm sighed and pulled the obelisk from his pouch. "I am Warchief Bagadibawm, and you are to take this and leave Alchiere at once."
Foulblood sheathed his saber and dumped what remained of his ale onto the sand. His eyes took on a beady, eager look that Bagadibawm didn’t like. "Oh, yes, the artifact. Dangerous thing, hey?"
He took the obelisk gingerly and held it up to examine it. "Obsidian, you think? Black jade, maybe?"

name: Name
body: "It is a thing of evil that must be disposed of at once," Bagadibawm said, growing increasingly alarmed at this strange trollkin’s behavior. Behind him rose the piercing warble of a firetongue warning croak. The Orgoth were near and no doubt more than a little singed after tangling with Mawga’Bawza. "Oh, right, right, right," Foulblood said, nodding. "Just curious." "The enemy is behind me." Bagadibawm pointed back into the trees. "Right behind me." Foulblood blinked and said nothing for a moment then seemed to come to his senses. "Oh, right, Definitely. Time to go. Don’t you worry, Baggybom, Commodore Foulblood and his doughty crew of cutthroats and villains will see the job done." Bagadibawm watched Commodore Foulblood walk, too slowly, back to his boats, holding the obelisk up like some kind of prize while his crew cheered and patted him on the back. They were somewhat swift about getting the boats into the water, for which Bagadibawm was thankful, but as he watched the commodore row back to his ship, he couldn’t help but think he had given the artifact to the world’s greatest fool.

name: Name
body:
Commodore Dario Foulblood had gathered his senior staff in his cabin to admire his latest acquisition. There was his first mate, Mr. Bogs, a doughty pyg cutthroat in a pin-sharp Llaelese naval officer’s uniform, his huge deck sweeper blunderbuss as outsized as his dubious opinion of his own battle prowess. Then came the Lochabash Brothers, three hulking trollkin dressed in mismatched bits of uniform from Mercarian League marines, their long rifles cocked over their shoulders as they stood at attention. Finally, there was Sully perched on a powder casque and painting Foulblood’s carpet with pelican guano. Sully was more mascot than crew, but the huge sea bird had learned to carry loads of bombs in his gular pouch and drop them on unsuspecting enemies. As such, he was immensely popular with the rank and file.
Foulblood set the Orgoth obelisk on his desk, the writhing runes casting a sickly crimson radiance across the wide-eyed faces of his officers. His spider monkey familiar, Payday, raced up his arm and onto his shoulder, hooting in appreciation. "Get a close look, lads."

name: Name
body: "That the thing Madrak wanted you to get from that froggy, sir?" one of the Lochabash Brothers asked. Foulblood thought it might be Durgal, but in truth he couldn’t really tell them apart. "It is indeed," Foulblood said, took a pull from his tankard, and wiped the foam from his lips. "The great chieftain entrusted me to handle this affair because no one is more capable in battle, business, or boudoir than Commodore Dario Foulblood, eh?" "Oh, aye, sir," Mr. Bogs said. "No two ways about it. You’n the crew of the Golden Empress can put paid to any task." "Just so," Foulblood said, grinning. "But, uh, beggin’ your pardon, sir, what did Madrak want you to do with it?" One of the other Lochabash Brothers asked. Foulblood hazarded a guess it was Konor this time. "To safeguard it of course," Foulblood replied. "And, well, to dispose of it when the time comes." "Dispose of it how?" Mr. Bogs asked and reached over the desk to poke at the obelisk with a stunted finger. Foulblood slapped the pyg’s hand away with his tankard. "Madrak left that to my discretion, but dispose can mean a lot of things, as you well know. It might mean dropping into the ocean. It might mean feeding to old Sully there." At the mention of his name, Sully squawked and opened his cavernous beak in hopes a fish or a bomb might be forthcoming. "It might mean placing it in the hands of one of the most powerful nations in the Iron Kingdoms. For an appropriate fee, of course."

name: Name
body: "I was wonderin’ why we’d sailed into the Gulf of Cygnar," Mr. Bogs said with a leering grin. "Just your plan coming to fruition, eh, Commodore." "Indubitably," Foulblood said. The cabin suddenly shook with a concussive explosion. A hue and cry went up from the crew on the main deck. Foulblood drew his cutlass, finished his ale in one last great pull, and grabbed the obelisk from his desk. "But, of course, dropping it in the ocean is still an option." *** The Golden Empress had attempted to outrun the Orgoth vessel, but the enemy ship was faster and closed the gap with both alacrity and precision. The red-sailed marauder had pulled alongside Foulblood’s ship and was unloading cannon fire into her at point-blank range, but the fire and explosions were just the precursor to the enemy’s main objective. Boarding ramps were swiftly lowered, and a horde of bestial terrors surged across. The Lochabash Brothers had already organized trollkin riflemen into a firing line, but even the rippling shudder of two dozen long rifles discharging hardly fazed the Orgoth boarding action. The enemy poured onto the Golden Empress in a howling whirlwind of destruction, surging into melee, effectively removing the trollkin guns from the equation.

name: Name
body: "Should we wake Chum, sir?" Mr. Bogs said at Foulblood’s knee. Foulblood wrinkled his nose at the mere mention of the Golden Empress’ enormous deepborn dire troll. Fearsome in combat and even more fearsome to the nose, Chum exuded a stench that was nearly as potent as his gaping shark-toothed maw. Foulblood reached out and touched Chum’s mind. It was like sinking into a maelstrom of hunger and rage. Come on, you reeking mountain of fish slop. There’s work to do. A succession of thuds and crashes from below followed Foulblood’s summons, then a briny stink washed across the deck as Chum burst from the hold with a shattering roar. The deepborn dire troll gripped a flail composed of anchor chains and sea mines in one meaty fist and the flopping, horrific form of a fang-mawed dragonfish in the other. It cast about for its first target, and Foulblood quickly clamped down on Chum’s rage to keep it from eating his crew. Payday, perched upon Foulblood’s shoulder as always, hid his tiny face against the nape of his master’s neck to escape Chum’s stomach-churning odor.

name: Name
body:
"Time to get stuck in, eh, Mr. Bogs?" Foulblood said. "Lead from the front and all that."
The pyg first mate hefted his deck sweeper and nodded. "Couldn’t agree more, sir."
***
Foulblood slashed the head from an Orgoth warrior and kicked the corpse over the side. Another marauder took his comrade’s place and launched a flurry of blows with an axe in one hand and a sword in the other. Both weapons glowed with fell green light and made a low howling sound as they sliced through the air.
Foulblood managed to parry the axe, though the force of the blow nearly ripped his cutlass from his grip. He threw himself to the side to avoid the sword, grimacing as the edge of the blade slashed a bloody furrow across his right leg. He turned his parry into a desperate riposte and ran his foe through. Even mortally wounded, the Orgoth warrior refused to give up the fight, and as he sank to the deck, he dropped his axe and pawed at Foulblood’s belt, trying to get at the pouch containing the obelisk. Foulblood jerked his weapon free and split the groping Orgoth’s skull.

name: Name
body:
"I knew I should have left this bloody thing in my cabin," Foulblood said under his breath and pressed a hand to the wound on his leg. It had become painfully clear the Orgoth were after the obelisk, which he had foolishly carried into combat. He might as well have painted a target on his chest.
The thundering blast of Mr. Bogs’ deck sweeper brought him back to more pressing issues, and he turned to see the pyg reloading his cannon-like rifle, the splattered remains of a pair of Orgoth warriors smeared across the deck in front of him.
Foulblood had sent Chum to bolster the Lochabash Brothers as they fought to stem the tide of Orgoth boarders. The dire troll was gleefully biting the heads and limbs off any enemy that wandered too close or reducing others to gory paste with thundering blasts from his mine flail if they tried keeping their distance.
The effects of the four pints of ale he’d consumed in his cabin were beginning to wear off, and Foulblood took advantage in the slight lull in combat to pluck a bottle of Rhulic uiske from his belt, bite the cork free, and take a long swig. He passed the bottle to Mr. Bogs.

name: Name
body: Bogs took an impressive pull, smacked his lips, and handed the bottle back. "This dwarven stuff’s got a bit more fire than that Khadoran swill, don’t it?" "Enough to give a whelp whiskers," Foulblood said. "Into the fray, sir?" "Now that we’re properly fortified, aye," Foulblood said, pointed his cutlass, and began slashing a meandering path down to where the Orgoth had boarded en masse and were giving his boys hell. A cry of "Foulblood is with us!" went up as the commander of the Golden Empress joined the melee. His plan was not all drunken bravado, however. He was now in sight of the Orgoth captain standing tall and fearsome on the main deck of his ship. The armored warrior wore a steel mask, and the flail he carried blazed with hellish fire. The warlord pointed at Foulblood and roared, "That one! Kill that one and bring me the key!" "You’ve drawn an audience, Commodore," Mr. Bogs said. "It would seem I have," Foulblood replied, reached into his pouch and drew out the obelisk. He held it up and shook it so the Orgoth commander could clearly see it. "We’ll draw the worst of the lot toward the prow. Chum and the lads can handle the rest."

name: Name
body:
In response, the Orgoth commander lifted his arms, the air around him shimmered like a heat mirage, and a sudden awful wailing rose over the battle. The bodies of fallen trollkin writhed on the deck and then disgorged streamers of howling energy that streaked across the deck and whirled around the Orgoth warlord in a haze of tenebrous power. He spoke a string of choking syllables, a guttural intonation that could not rightly be called words, and the weapons of his warriors became limned in shadowy power.
"Well, that’s not something you see every day," Foulblood said, the unfamiliar chill of dread clawing up his spine.
Mr. Bogs tugged at Foulblood’s sleeve, his eyes glassy with horror. "We’d best get moving, sir."
"I think we’d better had."
***

name: Name
body:
Foulblood had long believed his fortunes were as mercurial as the tides of the Meredius, and it was his duty to navigate those tides as best he could for himself and his crew. So, when he and Mr. Bogs reached the prow, and the Orgoth forces did not split and instead continued to slaughter his crew with wild abandon, he believed his fortunes were at low tide.
When the dragonspawn came hurtling out of the sky, proving that not only was fortune fickle but also damn creative, Foulblood wondered if he’d somehow managed to offend fate itself.
The new arrivals were winged amalgamations of serpentine flesh and shining steel, and Foulblood could not tell where organic creature ended and synthetic being began. They were led by a great brute who descended from the sky with a guttural roar, landing on the deck of the Orgoth ship near the masked warlord, twin blades as long as a trollkin is tall cutting a swathe of destruction through the enemy.
"What in Dhunia’s breath is that?" Mr. Bogs said, his mouth hanging open in stunned awe, his deck sweeper hanging from nerveless fingers.

name: Name
body:
Foulblood, too, was momentarily put off his guard by the shocking appearance of the dragonspawn. Luckily, Payday was more alert. The spider monkey screeched in alarm as a bestial Orgoth warrior barreled forward, sword raised. Payday snatched a bottle of Llaelese brandy from Foulblood’s belt, took a healthy shot, and spewed a stream of fine spirits straight into the Orgoth’s face, causing him to stagger back. Foulblood came back to his senses and gutted the half-blinded enemy, then he pulled Mr. Bogs back toward the edge of the prow.
Foulblood sheathed his cutlass and plucked Bogs’ deck sweeper from the pygmy troll’s grasp.
"If I can borrow this for a moment," he said, upended the weapon, and braced its butt against the deck. He then pulled out the obelisk and jammed the thing into the deck sweeper’s muzzle. He brought the rifle to his shoulder, cocked the hammer, and said, "I have no idea what you properly call those things, Mr. Bogs, but I’m going to call them an opportunity."
He aimed the deck sweeper directly at the Orgoth commander, now surrounded by winged dragonspawn, and pulled the trigger. That the deck sweeper didn’t immediately detonate was fortunate, that the obelisk flew in a straight true line and did not tumble was lucky, and that it struck the Orgoth commander in the middle of his breastplate was nothing short of miraculous.

name: Name
body: The Orgoth commander went down, and the dragonspawn fell upon him in a tide of slashing blades and talons. The Orgoth troops aboard the Golden Empress immediately raced back across the boarding ramps to aid their fallen leader. Foulblood handed the deck sweeper back to Mr. Bogs. "I think it might be time we were underway." *** Foulblood stood on the Golden Empress’ sterncastle, watching the Orgoth ship rapidly dwindle into the distance. Dark forms suddenly sprang up from the enemy ship and took to the air. The dragonspawn passed overhead, heading west toward the Wyrmwall Mountains. The brute leading them held something black and shining in his taloned hands. Mr. Bogs craned his neck to look at the dragonspawn speeding past. "That looks like . . ." "That looks like something that’s been properly disposed of," Foulblood said, "just like Madrak asked." "Oh, aye, sir, of course," Mr. Bogs said. "Oh, uh, we’ve collected all those weird, glowing swords and axes from the Orgoth we killed like you ordered. Put ’em in a pile. Bloody things are making an awful racket."

name: Name
body:
"They’re called fell blades, Mr. Bogs," Foulblood said. "There’s quite a market for them in Khador, you know."
"Oh?" The pyg first mate brightened. "I suppose we’re heading north then."
Foulblood rubbed his hands together and grinned. "You suppose correctly."
***
Vallyx lumbered through the labyrinthine tunnels of the hive, clutching the obelisk he’d taken from the Orgoth ship and reveling in the queer power of the thing. He could feel it racing up his arms, filling his head with visions of conquest.
He found Rhyas in the center of the hive, resting next to a newly birthed vipex. The serpentine warbeast lay amid the unused elements of its own genesis, both flesh and steel, and the magic of its creation hung in the air, a tangible pall of power.
"What have you brought me, Vallyx?" Rhyas said, beckoning her first creation forward.
"We sought out a powerful Orgoth warlord as you requested, but he fought us fiercely, and we were forced to retreat," Vallyx said and put the obelisk on the ground before his creator. "The Orgoth were battling with a force of trollkin over this."

name: Name
body:
Rhyas picked up the obelisk, closed her eyes, then suddenly dropped the artifact with a pained hiss.
"You have brought us calamity, Vallyx," she said, but there was no rancor in her tone.
Vallyx bowed his head. "Forgive me, Mother. I felt its power and believed it may be of use to us."
Rhyas reached out and caressed Vallyx’s horned head. "It may yet serve us. It is a key that unlocks a vault where terrible secrets have been hidden. Any foolish enough to liberate this power tempts annihilation."
"Then what shall we do with it?" Vallyx asked.
"Take it into Cygnar. Leave it where it can easily be found," Rhyas said. "Let our enemies be the ones tempted."
